q: To make a U-turn, you must be able to see at least how far in both directions?
a: 150 metres
e: Never make a U-turn unless you can see at least 150 m both ways.
s: Never make a U-turn unless you can see at least 150 metres in both directions.

q: You may not pass left of the centre line within how many metres of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel?
a: 30 metres
e: 30 m: the same as the no-passing distance at a pedestrian crossover.
s: Passing left of a centreline is not permitted 30 metres from a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

q: It is illegal to drive in reverse on a divided road with a speed limit over…
a: 80 km/h
e: That includes the shoulder. The only exception is helping someone in trouble.
s: It is illegal to drive in reverse on a divided road that has a speed limit of more than 80 km/h.

q: You're driving inside a roundabout. A car is waiting at the yield line to enter. Who has the right-of-way?
a: You do: don't stop except to avoid a collision
e: Once you're in the roundabout, you have the right-of-way over entering traffic.
s: Once you are in the roundabout, do not stop except to avoid a collision; you have the right-of-way over entering traffic.

q: You signal to change lanes. Must drivers in the other lane let you in?
a: No: they expect you to stay in your lane and to yield to them
w: Yes, a signal gives you the right-of-way
Yes, if you signal for 3 seconds
Only if they're slower than you
e: Even if you signal, other drivers expect you to yield the right-of-way.
s: Even if you signal, they expect you to yield the right-of-way.

q: On a two-lane road, a car is passing you in the oncoming lane, and oncoming traffic is getting close. What should you do?
a: Move to the right side of your lane and be ready to slow down to let the passing car in
w: Speed up so the passer drops back
Move left to block the passer
e: Help the passing driver get in front of you quickly to prevent a collision.
s: Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

q: You've stopped at a red light and want to turn right. A pedestrian is starting to cross in front of you. What do you do?
a: Wait for the pedestrian, then turn when the way is clear
w: Turn quickly before they reach your lane
Turn, since right on red is allowed
e: Right on red: complete stop, then yield to pedestrians and other road users.
s: Remember to signal your turn and yield to pedestrians and others using the road.

q: You're turning left from a one-way road onto a one-way road at a red light. Who must you yield to?
a: Pedestrians and traffic
w: No one; you have the right-of-way
e: Stop completely, then yield to pedestrians and traffic before turning.
s: You may turn left from a one-way road to a one-way road on a red light after coming to a complete stop and making sure the way is clear. Yield to pedestrians and traffic.

q: You're waiting in a two-way left-turn lane. An oncoming car is waiting in the same lane, in front of you, and blocks your view. What should you do?
a: Turn only when you are sure the way is clear
w: Turn quickly while the other car waits
Pass the other car in the centre lane
e: Cars from both directions use this lane. Only go when you're sure.
s: Only go when you are sure the way is clear.

q: On a highway where trucks can't use the far left lane, you're in the next lane over and a truck wants to pass. What should you do?
a: Move to the right-hand lane as soon as you can
w: Stay in your lane; the truck must wait
Move to the far left lane
Speed up so the truck can't pass
e: That lane is the truck passing lane.
s: If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

q: When the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass your vehicle, you must:
a: Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass.
w: Speed up so that passing is not necessary.
Move to the left to prevent passing.
Signal to the other driver not to pass.
e: Official MTO sample question. Never speed up when being passed.
s: When faster traffic wants to pass you, move to the right and let it pass in safety.

q: When may you pass on the RIGHT shoulder?
a: Only to pass a vehicle turning left, and only if the shoulder is paved
w: Whenever the shoulder is wide enough
e: Right shoulder: only around a left-turning vehicle, only if paved. Left shoulder: never.
s: You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved.

q: When may you pass on the LEFT shoulder?
a: Never
w: Only to pass a vehicle turning right
e: You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.
s: You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

q: Which of these is NOT a time when passing on the right is allowed?
a: On a two-lane, two-way road when the car ahead is slow
e: Passing on the right is allowed on multi-lane or one-way roads, and when passing a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.
s: You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

q: Do you have to wear your seatbelt while backing up?
a: No: you may take it off to turn and see, but buckle up before driving forward
e: It's one of the few times you may remove it, if you need to turn your body to see.
s: You don't have to wear a seatbelt while backing up.

q: Which of these is NOT allowed inside a roundabout?
a: Changing lanes
w: Watching for pedestrians as you exit
e: Don't change lanes in a roundabout. If you miss your exit, go around again.
s: Do not change lanes while in the roundabout.

q: Never change lanes in traffic without:
a: Giving proper signal and looking to make sure the move can be made safely.
w: Looking in the rear view mirror only.
Blowing your horn and looking to the rear.
Decreasing speed and giving correct signal.
e: Official MTO sample question. Mirror only isn't enough: shoulder check too.
s: Never change lanes without giving the proper signal and looking to make sure the move can be made safely.

q: You're stopped in the intersection, waiting to turn left. How should your front wheels be?
a: Straight, until you can actually make the turn
e: If you're hit from behind with your wheels turned left, you could be pushed into oncoming traffic.
s: When you are stopped at an intersection waiting for approaching traffic to clear, don't turn your steering wheel to the left until you can complete the turn.

q: To keep full control when turning a corner, when should you finish braking?
a: Before you turn the steering wheel
e: Try not to brake and steer at the same time.
s: To keep full control of the vehicle, finish braking before you turn the steering wheel.

q: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into its lane?
a: When you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your inside (rear-view) mirror
w: As soon as your back bumper is past its front bumper
When the other driver flashes their lights
e: Signal first, then return once its whole front shows in your rear-view mirror.
s: when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you are passing in your inside mirror, make the lane change

q: You're in the inside lane of a roundabout and you miss your exit. What should you do?
a: Keep going around until you reach your exit again
w: Stop and wait for a gap to cut across
e: Don't stop and don't change lanes in a roundabout.
s: If in the inside lane and you miss your exit, you must continue around until you meet your exit again.

q: You missed your turn. What is the simplest and safest way to turn around?
a: Drive around the block
w: Make a U-turn on a curve
Make a three-point turn on a hill
e: If driving around the block isn't possible, a U-turn or three-point turn may be needed.
s: The simplest and safest way is to drive around the block

q: Where is it illegal to make a U-turn?
a: On a curve, on or near a railway crossing or hilltop, or near a bridge or tunnel that blocks your view
w: On any road with two lanes
e: These places block your view. Also never where a sign says no U-turn.
s: It is illegal to make a U-turn on a curve in the road, on or near a railway crossing or hilltop, or near a bridge or tunnel that blocks your view.

q: How must you pass a streetcar?
a: On the right, unless you're on a one-way road
e: Pass streetcars on the right (except on one-way roads).
s: You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road.

q: At a roundabout, you want to turn left. Which lane should you use?
a: The left lane
e: Left lane = turn left or go straight. Right lane = turn right or go straight.
s: Use the left lane to turn left or to go straight.

q: When you are deciding whether or not to make a U-turn, your first consideration should be to check:
a: Traffic regulations.
w: Presence of trees, fire hydrants or poles near the curb.
e: Official MTO sample question. First make sure there's no sign forbidding it.
s: Before you make a U-turn, check to make sure there is no sign saying not to.
